anomaly_def.Name: Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Critical engine settings (memory pools, checkpoint cadence, parallelism limits, etc.) are mis-tuned for the hardware or workload, so the bottleneck originates from the parameters themselves rather than from any intrinsic resource shortage.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : The database or log storage layer runs out of free bytes in data, temp, or archive locations, causing space-allocation failures and blocking growth or write activity.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes drive host CPU utilization to sustained saturation, exhausting compute cycles and lengthening run-queue wait time for all work.

When these three root causes co-exist, the system exhibits an intertwined failure pattern: frequent checkpoints or aggressive background writers (from poor configuration) generate surges of I/O and log activity that rapidly consume the remaining disk space, while simultaneously driving CPU to 100 % as the engine spends extra cycles on checkpoint processing, log archiving retries, space-error handling, and repeated scan or sort re-tries in shrinking temp areas. Applications may see a mixture of space-exhaustion errors, sudden latency spikes, timeouts, and alternating periods of near-idle disks (due to write throttling) and CPU run-queue waits. Monitoring views show mismatched indicators—high CPU and checkpoint/write wait events despite low actual I/O throughput, plus accelerating free-space depletion and recurrent autovacuum/autopurge backlogs.

Causally, mis-set configuration parameters (too small buffer pools, short checkpoint intervals, oversized parallelism) inflate write-amplification and log generation, pushing storage toward its capacity ceiling. As free space dwindles, the engine triggers more frequent checkpoints and log switches, which further raise CPU demand and intensify space pressure. Space errors force repeated allocation retries and rollback/redo processing, again consuming CPU. The resulting feedback loop—parameter-driven churn → space exhaustion → error handling → CPU saturation—escalates quickly, degrading both throughput and stability across transactional and analytical workloads.

entry.official_definition: Specifies how long transmitted data may remain unacknowledged before the TCP connection is forcibly closed.
entry.trigger_condition: TCP data sent by PostgreSQL remains unacknowledged longer than tcp_user_timeout on systems supporting TCP_USER_TIMEOUT.
entry.workload_impact: The TCP connection is forcibly closed.
entry.default_behavior: Default value is 0, selecting the operating system default.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
